mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last two weeks (from -53.1 to -40.6), indicating an accelerating recovery trend in discretionary mobility that will continue to push RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks as the recovery momentum persists.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -53.1 at t-2w to -40.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days despite the two-week upward trend observed at decision time.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 10 percentage points above baseline (crossing a behavioral threshold indicating reduced home-confinement), households resume discretionary outings, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below +10 points from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 14.3 at t-2w to 9.9 at t-0w, crossing below 10
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 14 days even though RESIDENTIAL remains below the +10 threshold for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility (both rose in the last week) jointly signal restored commuting and transit-dependent errand activity, which compounds to produce a larger increase in RETAIL_REC than either series alone would predict over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -43.6 to -36.4 and TRANSIT rose from -47.1 to -37.1 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 28 days is no greater than the growth predicted by either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT alone, or RETAIL_REC declines despite joint increases in both series.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rebound in PARKS mobility (from -43.9 to -24.1 over two weeks) signals relaxation of outdoor gathering restrictions under an easing-restrictions regime; this policy loosening spills over into retail and recreation activity, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 15 points over two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS increased from -43.9 at t-2w to -24.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days despite PARKS sustaining its sharp increase, or the regime is later identified as tightening rather than easing.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility exhibits a consistent weekly cadence correlated with RETAIL_REC due to shared shopping-trip seasonality; the recent narrowing of the GROCERY_PHARM deficit (from -28.6 to -18.9) foreshadows a parallel near-term uptick in RETAIL_REC within one week due to synchronized consumer shopping cycles.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -28.6 at t-2w to -18.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within the next 7 days despite GROCERY_PHARM continuing its improving trend.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility drops more than 10 points week-on-week, it signals renewed public caution about crowded public spaces, which suppresses discretionary retail visits and lowers RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -44.4 to -47.1 between t-3w and t-2w, a drop exceeding 10 points is possible under renewed caution
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat within the next 7 days despite a TRANSIT drop exceeding 10 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, any week-on-week decline in PARKS mobility signals renewed policy limits on outdoor and public activity, which historically precedes broader declines in RETAIL_REC within two weeks as restrictions cascade to retail settings.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -39.9 at t-3w to -43.9 at t-2w before later recovering
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 14 days despite a PARKS week-on-week decline under a tightening-restrictions regime.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of rising WORKPLACES and falling RESIDENTIAL mobility reflects a coordinated shift away from home-centered routines toward out-of-home activity, and their combined momentum amplifies the upward pull on RETAIL_REC more than either series alone over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -37.3 to -36.4 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 11.6 to 9.9 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days despite concurrent WORKPLACES increase and RESIDENTIAL decrease persisting across the period.
